rendered:
Here are the optimized conditions reported:

1. Cysteine concentration: 75 μM[1]. The CD intensity of L-HGNRs was highest at this level across a tested range of 45 to 120 μM[2].
2. Au/Ag growth solution volume: 80 μL[3]. The paper names a cysteine concentration of 75 μM and a growth solution volume of 80 μL[4] as the settings used to prepare BA@L-HGNRs.
4-MPBA[5] concentration: 165 μM[6]. CD intensity peaked at this concentration and then dropped slightly at higher levels. Probes made at this concentration also stayed spectrally stable after being redispersed in NH4HCO3 buffer. Raising the concentration up to 225 μM[7] changed the CD signal only a little.
NaCl concentration: 65 mM[8]. This was optimized using P. aeruginosa as the model bacterium. The ΔCD response rose between 25 mM to 65 mM[9], then fell slightly and levelled off at higher salt concentrations.
